articles.title: Dutch GP Sprint Qualifying: George Russell claims pole position with title rivals Kimi Antonelli, Lewis Hamilton on back foot
articles.summary: The newly-engaged George Russell bounces back to form with Zandvoort Sprint pole from Lando Norris and Charles Leclerc; Kimi Antonelli damaged car on his first lap; watch the Sprint on Saturday at 11am (build-up from 10am) with Qualifying at 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
On F1's first day back on track after the sport's four-week summer break, Russell claimed his third Sprint pole in five attempts this season as his final SQ3 lap of 1:11.567 beat McLaren's Lando Norris and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc to the head of the weekend's first Zandvoort grid by under a tenth of a second.

But championship leader Antonelli was only fifth quickest in the other Mercedes, the Italian teenager's session compromised after he damaged his car in a trip through the gravel on his first lap of SQ1.

Hamilton, who is second to Antonelli in the standings, qualified only seventh in the second Ferrari after earlier promise on Friday faded.

Hamilton trails Antonelli by 50 points in the Drivers' Championship, with Russell a further nine points adrift. Points are on offer to the top-eight finishers in Saturday's 24-lap Sprint, which starts at 11am on Sky Sports F1 , with eight for the winner.

Russell got engaged to his long-time partner Carmen Montero Mundt during F1's break and quipped on Mercedes team radio after his Sprint pole was confirmed: "Nice one! Must be a bit lighter after that engagement ring!"

Oscar Piastri took fourth in the second McLaren, just 0.009s back on pole himself, with Max Verstappen sixth for Red Bull at his home event - but half a second away from the front amid a disappointing opening day for Red Bull.

Indeed, Verstappen and seventh-placed Hamilton lapped closer to Alpine's Pierre Gasly - whose car has the Enstone team's sole upgrade this weekend - than the polesitter.

Eighth-placed Gasly led the midfield fight ahead of Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto in ninth and Racing Bulls' Arvid Linbdlad in 10th.

Lindblad denied Liam Lawson, his usual Racing Bulls' team-mate but who is racing for the senior Red Bull team this weekend in place of the injured Isack Hadjar, the last top-10 berth on the final laps of SQ2

Lawson, who had two ill-fated races for Red Bull at the start of last season, outpaced Verstappen in the first session but lost out on a SQ3 berth by three tenths of a second.

The New Zealander will start just ahead of Yuki Tsunoda, the driver who is standing in for him this weekend at Racing Bulls, with the Japanese qualifying 12th on his first F1 race weekend since December.

Fernando Alonso qualified last in the Aston Martin - which features Honda's long-awaited first engine upgrade as well as a second round of aerodynamic revisions - after a problem with his AMR26's straight-line mode cost him crucial lap time. The Spanish veteran had finished 12th fastest in the only practice session.

Russell 'really happy to come back' as Antonelli mistake proves costly

Russell's pole position lap at the end of SQ3 came as something of a surprise given the Briton had only lapped fifth and fourth-fastest respectively in the first two knockout segments, two tenths off the pace, with Ferrari and McLaren appearing to have the legs on championship leaders Mercedes.

But Russell proved a more competitive proposition on the mandatory, and single, soft-tyre runs of the final phase to deny McLaren rival Norris the fastest time.

"It was a tough end to the first half of the year and I'm really happy to come back," said Russell, who scored only six points in the two races before the summer break.

"The lap felt really good. It all came together really nicely. It's always difficult these Sprint Qualifyings with just one shot on the soft tyre. The track always takes a step, the grip takes a step.

"McLaren look quick, Ferrari look quick but I'm glad to pull it off when it matted."

Unusually Antonelli did not finish in the top four of any of the three qualifying segments, confirming afterwards that his slide wide through the gravel at the penultimate corner on his first timed lap of SQ1 had damaged the underside of his W17.

"Oh yeah, [there was] big time [damage]. I had a couple of holes in the floor," Antonelli said.

"When I came in, they initially said it was a loss of 25 [downforce] points. They tried to repair as much as possible, but definitely the damage was still there. I was struggling a lot in the low-speed [corners].

"It is what it is. It was a little bit too much entry speed in the last corner on that first lap. I lost the rear and went through the gravel, and that was pretty much it.

"And then obviously it was not easy to build the confidence back. But still decently close, and we'll have another go tomorrow."

articles.title: Alonso y unas mejoras que están verdes: "Es inmaduro, tuvimos problemas de motor"
articles.standfirst: El asturiano vivió una SQ1 infernal y su sprint queda condicionado por completo
articles.summary: El asturiano vivió una SQ1 infernal y su sprint queda condicionado por completo
articles.body: Las mejoras de Aston Martin todavía están… verdes. El juego de palabras puede ser válido después de un viernes del Gran Premio de los Países Bajos que enseñó que la Fórmula 1 tiene secretos en cada punto a tratar. Fernando Alonso saldrá 22° y último a un sprint (12:00 horas, DAZN) que podría presentarse como una oportunidad, pero mantiene la tarea de tener que trabajar más y más. Es su debe. Alonso vivió una clasificación sprint de desastre. Tenía tres intentos, y ni el coche estuvo fino ni las vueltas pudieron salir entre una descartada, una pequeña salida y la tercera sin el rendimiento adecuado. El coche sí que estaba en posiciones de Q2 holgada tras el primer libre, pero la clasificación corta enseñó que hay más cosas que poner a punto. Empiezan en el motor, la gran novedad que Honda traía. Es mejor, no hay dudas. Pero tiene que optimizarse. “Nos pasó de todo en la clasificación. El libre fue más o menos bien, pero después sufrimos problemas en el motor. Son de manejabilidad, pues el motor empujaba en las rectas y era difícil poder frenar el coche debido a esa situación al parecer que sobreentregaba”, relató el asturiano a los medios oficiales de la Fórmula 1. Hubo más lío. También su coche tuvo un problema en la aerodinámica activa y el AMR26 no era manejable al fallar en la parte trasera. “No me funcionaba el modo recta y no podía abrir el alerón trasero durante las zonas de SM. Las vueltas eran muy complicadas”, precisaba. El plano que vivió su coche enseña todo. Insalvable y demoledor. Pero no se puede ser negativo de forma radical. El coche mejora y hay una herramienta sobre la que Aston ya puede construir. Pero no será en el sprint de Holanda. “Es un paso adelante, pero es temprano y llevamos poco tiempo y quizá es todo un poco inmaduro. Cosas como los controles. Y al ser un fin de semana sprint pues no tienes los tres entrenamientos de otros Grandes Premios y no se puede perfeccionar el paquete antes de vivir una situación como la clasificación. Así que utilizaremos la carrera corta para entender cosas”, cerró.

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Klassleader looks well treated in the Ebor
articles.summary: William Haggas and Tom Marquand will be hoping Klassleader can regain the winning thread on the final day of York's Ebor Festival; Hollie Doyle believes the son of Lope De Vega can make it two from two on the Knavesmire
articles.body:
If you're willing to forgive his run in the Old Newton Cup at Newmarket last month then Klassleader must be on your shortlist for the £500,000 Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (3.35) at York on Saturday.

My husband Tom (Marquand) felt he simply didn't handle the undulations that day but the way he justified favouritism in a mile and a half handicap at this track back in May gives me the impression he's well treated on a mark of 98.

Alan King's Daiquiri Bay had his moment in the sun in the Copper Horse Stakes at Royal Ascot and looks sure to go well over this extra quarter mile. He's no stranger to The Knavesmire, having finished a gallant third over course and distance in last season's Melrose Stakes, and has been handed a good low draw.

Another open to improvement is the Willie Mullins runner Love Me Tender , a fascinating recruit from Germany who has winning form in soft ground. That said, William Buick's mount has something to prove on his handicap debut over a trip he has never run over.

Zavateri can upset older rivals in Group One feature

I'd love to see Eve Johnson Houghton's Zavateri win the Group One Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (3.00). He's a proven performer at this level and a relatively fresh horse whose run behind Bow Echo in the Sussex Stakes was encouraging.

Zavateri was smart enough to win the Group One National Stakes at two, beating Gstaad in yielding ground, and looks a more appealing proposition than Godolphin's brilliant miler Notable Speech .

The faster they go the better for him on his first try over seven furlongs but, although he sets a tough standard on ratings, he has something to prove after disappointing on that much stiffer track at Ascot in the Queen Anne, when he was beaten by Ten Bob Tony . Ed Walker's colt will revel in the conditions and can at least confirm the form.

Japan's classy entire Satono Reve is an interesting contender after his near miss in the Group One Jubilee at Royal Ascot. He tackles this trip for the first time but I'm more concerned about the soft ground for him as he's never encountered conditions so demanding.

Ireland can take the honours in the Group Three Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (1.50) at York with the reliable Geryon , who already has winning form at this level.

Ger Lyons's grey landed the Meld Stakes in decisive fashion over this 9f trip at Leopardstown this summer before going down with guns blazing in the Gordon Stakes at The Goodwood Festival.

Dropping back in distance is very much in his favour and slow ground holds no fears, as he showed when chasing home the classy Hawk Mountain in the Group Two Beresford Stakes as a two-year-old.

Market rival Damysus is another who likes to get his toe in and bumped into one in the Group Two York Stakes last month when he finished behind this week's Juddmonte International hero Item. The addition of cheekpieces could be a plus but he must give seven pounds to my fancy.

It was great to see my husband Tom and William Haggas win the Great Voltigeur on Wednesday with the gorgeous Maltese Cross and I'm hoping they can take another big staying prize with Infraad.

I loved the way he nailed a Class Two handicap at the Goodwood Festival last time, scoring in a manner that suggests he will enjoy the greater test of stamina in the Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (2.25) at York.

A seven-pound rise to 97 shouldn't impede a colt who looks a pattern performer in the making so I can see him getting the better of class dropper Limestone , who is the definitive Group winner in a handicap following his success in the Queen's Vase.

Giving so much weight to progressive types like Infraad demands plenty of Joseph O'Brien's star, though he won't be inconvenienced by the testing conditions - a comment that applies to Andrew Balding's easy ground Newbury winner Mythical Bay .

Air Force One is out to complete a memorable Ebor Festival double in the Sky Bet Constantine Handicap ( 4.10) after winning over the straight track in such game style on Wednesday and looks sure to go well, even with a five-pound penalty.

However, I'm a big fan of Tim Easterby's Red Spells Danger who arrives at The Knavesmire on the back of an impressive win in the Shergar Cup Sprint two weeks ago. He has a six-pound rise to overcome on slower ground but is progressive enough to find the answers.

David O'Meara's Toca Madera was third behind Air Force One on Day Two and also backs up quickly. He's a sprinter in form but just isn't nailing his races and may have to settle for another share of the place money.

Derby runner-up tops bill in Chester Marathon

Godolphin's By The Book and Charlie Johnston's Classic-placed Lazy Griff looks set to fight it out in the Listed Virgin Bet Chester Stakes (2.40) - one of seven races at The Roodee that are live on Sky Sports Racing on Saturday.

Championship leader Billy Loughnane partners this Meydan handicap winner who has run well in Group races this year without getting his head in front. He's a solid option but will have to pull out all the stops to deny Lazy Griff .

Charlie's colt was placed in both the English and Irish Derbies last year after finishing just a length and a half behind Epsom hero Lambourn in the Chester Vase. He didn't fire in the Goodwood Cup after making all to win a Listed race at Sandown in July but can prove a tough nut to crack from an attacking draw in stall three.

Drop back in trip no concern for Cracker

George Boughey's exciting Asuka has been dealt a tricky draw in the Class Two Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap (2.05) at Chester on Saturday.

Billy Loughnane will need to ride for luck from out in stall 12 if this smart colt is to complete a hat-trick on ground that will be slower than he's raced on so far.

A better option could be Richard Hughes' five-year-old Whip Cracker who, by contrast, has a much better draw in stall four and ran well at this track back in the spring. Conditions will hold no fears for him on his first try over this kind of trip since his novice win three years ago.

It felt so good to be back on a horse this week - even if it was a mechanical one at Oaksey House in Lambourn!

I had a session on the Equicizer as part of my on-going rehabilitation from the injuries I sustained in that fall at Bath back in May.

The team at Oaksey House continue to be a great support in my fight to regain full fitness, though it's still too early to say when I might be back in the saddle proper.

articles.title: George Russell: Mercedes driver says Dutch GP Sprint pole a good reminder of his talent as Kimi Antonelli bemoans car damage
articles.summary: George Russell edged out Lando Norris and Charles Leclerc for Sprint pole in Zandvoort; championship leader Kimi Antonelli fifth after damaging car; watch the Sprint on Saturday at 11am (build-up from 10am) with Qualifying for the Dutch GP at 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Having begun the season as the clear favourite for the drivers' title, Russell has endured a tumultuous campaign which has seen him unexpectedly outperformed by his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Antonelli arrived in Zandvoort, the first event after the sport's summer break, with a 50-point lead over Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton at the top of the Drivers' Championship, with Russell a further nine points adrift in third.

Knowing he needs a major turnaround to fight back in the title race, Russell made the perfect start on Friday by beating McLaren's Lando Norris to Sprint pole after Antonelli took himself out of contention by damaging his car in the gravel in the first part of the session.

Russell said: "It's been a little while since I've been top of the timesheets in any session. I can't even remember the last time.

"It's good to remind myself I've still got it and haven't forgotten how to drive. The break came at a good point."

Russell edged out Norris by four hundredths of a second, with Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and the other McLaren of Oscar Piastri also finishing within a tenth of the Brit's leading time.

"Of course it's only the Sprint," Russell added. "Qualifying will be the key one and McLaren look really fast and Ferrari look quick.

"It's been a real surprise to us as a team these past couple of races. We are in a good spot."

Russell appeared to run out of ideas as the summer break approached, with the 28-year-old publicly flip-flopping on whether his driving style was the reason he was struggling to match Antonelli, who is competing in just his second F1 season and only turns 20 two days after Sunday's race.

"I came into this weekend with a real open mind because I had no idea how it would go. My confidence level wasn't exactly at my highest," Russell said.

"I just tried to remember that feeling of what I needed from myself and the car - almost treating it like the first race of the season again and not overthink things. That seems to have worked well for me.

"It's very difficult to actually put those words into action but I know when I'm in the right frame of mind, come Q3 I can always deliver, it's just ensuring I'm in the right frame of mind ahead of that point."

Antonelli says 'big-time' damage cost him

Antonelli had topped the weekend's sole practice to establish himself as favourite for Sprint pole but made an unnecessary error in the first part of qualifying.

Pushing hard on his first lap in SQ1, Antonelli lost control of his car at the final corner and actually did well to stay pointing forward and avoid becoming beached in the gravel.

Antonelli was able to comfortably advance through SQ1 and SQ2 despite Mercedes finding holes in the floor of his car, but was two tenths off Russell in SQ3 as he finished fifth.

Asked if the damage had impacted him, Antonelli told Sky Sports F1 : "Oh yeah, big time. I had a couple of holes in the floor.

"When I came in, they initially said it was a loss of 25 [downforce] points. They tried to repair as much as possible, but definitely the damage was still there. I was struggling a lot in the low-speed [corners].

"It is what it is. It was a little bit too much entry speed in the last corner on that first lap. I lost the rear and went through the gravel, and that was pretty much it.

"And then obviously it was not easy to build the confidence back. But still decently close, and we'll have another go tomorrow."

Wolff: Pressure off Russell's shoulders after engagement!

Mercedes chief Toto Wolff suggested Russell may have benefitted from getting engaged to his long-term partner Carmen Montero Mundt during the summer break.

Wolff told Sky Sports F1 : "George is coming back. I think he feels so much pressure is off his shoulders after she accepted his marriage proposal!

"Some solid work on the day to day, he put the dots together and had a very good lap."

Wolff appeared to play down the extent of the damage to Antonelli's car, suggesting Mercedes had largely repaired the issue ahead of SQ3.

"Kimi lost 20 points [of downforce] with a hole in the floor but we managed to patch it up and it looked like it was completely intact afterwards," Wolff said.

"The gaps are so close and he made a little bit of a mistake at Turn 11, pushing too hard on the entry, and it can go quickly."

articles.title: York Ebor Festival: Bacio blazes a trail to win Nunthorpe Stakes as Arapaho Gold takes Gimcrack Stakes honours
articles.summary: Wesley Ward had hit the post with both Acapulco and Lady Aurelia in the past but the Keeneland-based trainer finally got his hands on the Nunthorpe prize as ace sprinter Bacio blazed a trail on the Knavesmire; Arapaho Gold takes Gimcrack Stakes honours at York
articles.body:
While the popular Keeneland-based trainer has enjoyed 13 winners at Royal Ascot, success on the Knavesmire has proved elusive, having saddled Acapulco to finish second in 2015 and come even closer two years later through Lady Aurelia, with Frankie Dettori memorably celebrating passing the post only to find he had actually been beaten a nose by Marsha.

Bacio was the 3/1 favourite to go one better under Juan Hernandez following a brilliant victory in the Palace of Holyroodhouse at the Royal meeting in June and pre-race concerns about the rain-softened ground soon proved unfounded as the three-year-old flew out of the starting stalls.

He had most of his rivals struggling to keep up from halfway and never really looked in any danger of being reeled in, passing the post a length and a quarter clear of Starlust.

No sooner had Hernandez piloted an aeroplane up the York straight he had to run back to the weighing room as he needed to make a sharp exit, with a 6.30pm flight back to America from Heathrow to Los Angeles ahead of the Pacific Classic at Del Mar.

To make sure he made that flight, Hernandez first had to take a helicopter ride from the middle of the Knavesmire to Heathrow and he did not have a minute to spare.

While running back for a brief presentation of the trophies from the Queen, he said: "The horse was giving everything and he'd trained really good.

"He shipped really well, I know a lot of people were worried about the ground for him but he didn't know that.

"He ran great, he broke out of the gate really well, really sharp and he was ready to go. When the gate opened, he was all fire. He was trying to go too early, but I was able to take him back a little bit and save him for the last part.

"He won the race from the gate. Everyone here has done such a great job with the horse. I'm really happy, this race is for America and all my family. Thank you guys!"

Arapaho Gold stretched his unbeaten record to four with victory in the Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack Stakes.

The Michael Dods-trained gelding won a couple of low-key races at Thirsk either side of being withdrawn after playing up in the stalls at Beverley, since when he had successfully graduated to Listed company in the Rose Bowl at Newbury.

He faced another step up in class for this prestigious Group Two contest, but proved more than up to the task in the hands of Connor Beasley, briefly coming under pressure before getting himself organised and finishing strongly to repel Final Objective by three-quarters of a length at 2/1.

Darlington-based Dods has enjoyed some of the best days of his career at York, having saddled Mecca's Angel to win her second Nunthorpe on this day 10 years ago, while he also sent out the popular sprinter Dakota Gold to win on the Knavesmire six times.

"Once he was out and running I was happy. At halfway he was looking for a bit of room, but once the room came he really quickened up," said Dods.

"Connor just said the last 100 yards he gave him some feel the way he quickened away from them. He's a good horse, this was a big step up and he's taken everything in his stride. When we've wanted him to step up he has and he has stepped up again there. He's just some horse isn't he?"

On future plans, Dods added: "He'll go to the Mill Reef (at Newbury) now and that will probably be it for the season and we'll see where we go next year.

"He's got the speed for six furlongs as you've just seen and I don't think you'll see any problems getting seven. He quickens up and he gallops. It's an interesting problem (planning), but we'll deal with it. He's an exciting horse to have and it's brilliant that we've got him in the yard.

"We've had a lot of luck at York, but this is right up there with the two Mecca's Angel wins and winning that is unbelievable."

Richard Brown, racing advisor to Wathnan Racing, who own the runner-up Final Objective, said: "It was a massive run, it's one where you are delighted because the horse has run a huge race.

"A furlong out I thought he was coming to win, he hasn't been straightforward and Hamad (Al Jehani) has done a great job training this horse and that is a career best, so we'll keep him busy.

"He wandered about when he won at Thirsk last week and he has done again, so I think we'll pop a pair of cheekpieces on.

"There's a race in France, the Prix Eclipse, that we could look at, but we'll all have a sit down and see what might be best for him."

Adrian Keatley said of the third home, Hell Of A Spin: "He's a hardy little horse who tries his heart out and he's running consistently well in these good races.

"You'd like to think there's a nice one in him one of these days, I don't think the trip or ground were a concern for him, it was just the winner quickened away.

"He's been placed in a Molecomb and Gimcrack now. There could be a race in France towards the back-end for him - we'll keep trying."

articles.title: Kevin Blake's Ebor Festival tips: Sky Sports Racing expert looks ahead to day four at York with three selections
articles.summary: Day four of the York Ebor Festival takes place on Saturday and is headlined by the Sky Bet Ebor Handicap; Sky Sports Racing's Kevin Blake has put up three selections on the card on the Knavesmire
articles.body:
York have been unlucky with the weather this week, and the softening ground has created some extra challenges, but all being well we can hopefully finish the week on a high.

The Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (1:50) is the first race of interest, and one that looks overpriced is the Hamad Al Jehani-trained Archivist . Long-term readers may recall that I put him up as my selection in the Royal Hunt Cup at Royal Ascot and while it didn't work out for him on the day, he gained compensation on his very next start when overcoming what was considered a near impossible draw of 20 in the Golden Mile at Glorious Goodwood.

Not only did he overcome his draw, he did it with a bit to spare and that performance signalled his readiness to be competitive at stakes level. This course and distance should suit him well and any ease in the ground shouldn't be overly inconvenient for him. He is drawn a little wider than ideal, but that is bearable given his price is so big. A big run from him wouldn't at all surprise.

The Sky Bet Constantine Handicap (4:10) is another extremely tough sprint handicap, but I'm game to have a swing at the Andrew Balding-trained Dance In The Storm . The manner in which the betting markets have been so positive about her in her four starts this season has strongly suggested that she is considered better than a handicapper.

While she has won two of her four starts over seven furlongs this season, she has very much been shaping as though she is worth a try at this shorter trip. She has a career-high mark to overcome, but this different distance could well unlock notable further improvement. She is a really interesting contender and warrants support.

The final selection of the week comes in the concluding Sky Bet Dav Reid Finale Handicap (5:20), and it is the Ger Lyons-trained Diego El Queso . The four-year-old has a progressive profile, winning a handicap at Leopardstown in good style back in April prior to having an absence of 12 weeks that suggests he may have had a hold up.

He returned to action with a tremendous run to finish second to Thread Of Gold in a valuable handicap back at Leopardstown and that form has been well advertised by the winner since then. He was well fancied for a similar race to this at Glorious Goodwood, but the race went wrong for him, yet he still managed to catch the eye in finishing sixth.

He is capable of better than he was able to show there and with both this course and distance and the ease in the ground all promising to suit him, he can be expected to make a bold bid for compensation.

articles.title: NASCAR Legend Kurt Busch Opens Up on Brother Kyle's Death in Emotional Interview
articles.summary: NASCAR Hall of Famer Kurt Busch shared an account of his final moments with his late brother Kyle Busch in an emotional interview aired Friday on TODAY.
articles.body:
NASCAR Hall of Famer Kurt Busch shared an account of his final moments with his late brother Kyle Busch in an emotional interview aired Friday on TODAY.

Busch described gathering with other family members at the hospital after his brother suffered a medical emergency while using a racing simulator in May.

Kyle Busch died the next day after suffering what his family described as complications resulting from sepsis following pneumonia.

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

"I was there at the hospital. I was there all day. Hoping, praying. Hoping for a turnaround," Busch told TODAY 's Craig Melvin.

Busch said his father, Tom Busch, did not go into the hospital room because he "wanted to remember him in the way he wanted to remember him."

During his own visit to the hospital room, Busch said he told his brother: "I got you, man. C'mon. I got you. I've got you, c'mon, be strong."

He wiped away tears as he added, "Just wasn't fair."

Busch told Melvin he has since been mentoring his brother's 11-year-old son Brexton Busch.

"He's a prodigy. He was on the gas even before all of this," Busch said about Brexton. "He can be a big star in the world of motorsports. He's 11, but he's already racing like an 18 year old, so it's time to be around a bit more."

About what he missed most about his brother, Busch said, "I loved, on track, him and I were carbon copies of each other.

"I just miss the on-track comradery. We could speak on track without saying a word... I miss the words that we never spoke to each other and the vibe that we had on track."

Kyle Busch competed in his final NASCAR Cup Series race 11 days before his death. The television broadcast said at the time he had been struggling with a sinus cold, per Steve Reed of the Associated Press.

He holds an all-time record 63 Cup wins along with 234 career victories across NASCAR's three national series and will be a lock to join his brother in the NASCAR Hall of Fame as soon as be becomes eligible for induction.

articles.title: Todo a Sainz: "Su nivel es de campeón del mundo, pelear por podios... y más"
articles.standfirst: James Vowles cuenta qué ha llevado a firmar su histórica ampliación con el madrileño con uno de los contratos más destacados de la parrilla
articles.summary: James Vowles cuenta qué ha llevado a firmar su histórica ampliación con el madrileño con uno de los contratos más destacados de la parrilla
articles.body: Aunque en la parrilla sprint (12:00 horas, DAZN) de cara al sábado del Gran Premio de los Países Bajos no luzca su puesto (18º), y tampoco vaya a mejorar mucho la cosa de cara a la carrera (15:00 horas, domingo), nadie en el paddock de la Fórmula 1 quita los focos de Carlos Sainz. Su renovación fue la gran noticia justo antes de volver a la acción, después llegó la de Max Verstappen por una millonada (un montante total de más de 400 millones) y el español estrena un estatus que sólo tienen los mejores pilotos de la parrilla. Es uno de ellos, queda claro. Así lo creen en Williams, que reivindican con orgullo su vinculación con el 55. "Nos preocupaba perderlo porque es un piloto con nivel de campeonato mundial. Se merece la oportunidad de luchar por podios y más", apuntó su jefe, James Vowles. El mismo dirigente que maravilló en 2025 y ahora se enfrenta a un reto total. No parece que sea en el corto plazo, pues el 2026 se dará casi por perdido tras el subidón que volverá a llegar en Bakú. Pero sí de cara al futuro. "No le dimos la oportunidad de pelear por todo pese a que teníamos la visión clara. El paso atrás tiene el riesgo de poder perder a los pilotos, pero agradezco que se mantengan al lado. Sin buscar culpables, ofreciéndose a buscar soluciones y lo que faltaba. Esto forma parte de ellos", añadió. Los elogios siempre han existido y refuerzan a Sainz, pero Williams también debe encontrar pasos adelante para construir. El español decía que sí que tienen las herramientas y en Grove son directos: van a volver al frente. "Demostramos todo lo que hacemos para solucionar los problemas, el giro que dimos y el futuro. Estamos muy lejos, pero sí hay cambios y una trayectoria correcta a seguir. Mejoramos en los circuitos, aunque no seamos capaces de sumar. Pero enseñamos una combinación de procesos, personas, sistemas y estructuras que demuestran el buen camino", analizó el británico. Carlos, eso sí, no olvida lo que ocurrió en el inicio de curso. El coche nació mal desde el inicio, con sobrepeso y la incapacidad de recibir evoluciones importantes. En Gran Bretaña todo pareció más negativo al encontrar mejoras sin un salto cualitativo en el monoplaza, aunque visto en perspectiva no lo era tanto. "Creíamos que no mejorábamos, pero sí. Lo que ocurre es que el ritmo de desarrollo es alto y hay más problemas en el coche", indicó Vowles. Y tiene claro que le puede pasar a todo el mundo. "Nadie te puede garantizar que no se equivocarán. Hay miles de decisiones en invierno y tomarás el camino equivocada con varias erróneas. Es lo que te marca ganar o no", añadió. Las palabras de cara al futuro son positivas y el trabajo ya ha empezado, pero los objetivos no pueden ser desmesurados. Ni deben. "No voy a prometer nada a nadie, ningún equipo campeón lo hace. Quiero demostrar que hay profundidad que antes no existía en sistemas, herramientas, proceso y personal para detectar los problemas", sentenció Vowles. Un mensaje a Sainz y el futuro. Es su piloto y la confianza es mutua. Ahora queda construir todo lo demás.

articles.title: Aston Martin, unas mejoras con deberes y con Alonso desde el pit-lane
articles.standfirst: Los coches de Silverstone no pasaron de la SQ1 cuando su ritmo real podría asentarlos en la media tabla
articles.summary: Los coches de Silverstone no pasaron de la SQ1 cuando su ritmo real podría asentarlos en la media tabla
articles.body: En Aston Martin se trabaja sabiendo negociar entre las expectativas y la realidad. Si bien eran rotundos para defender su salto adelante a partir de los Grandes Premios de Hungría y de los Países Bajos, jamás habían lanzado mensajes excesivamente optimistas con puestos, cálculos o predicciones innecesarias. El viernes de Zandvoort, además, fue el punto claro en el que también se reforzó esa idea. “Está todo inmaduro”, decía Fernando Alonso. Tanto el asturiano como su compañero Lance Stroll sabían que había ritmo para mucho más, pero a la hora de la verdad no apareció. Y no fue un motivo único, falló casi todo en el paquete del coche. El motor Honda ha mejorado significativamente con su actualización, pero los pilotos demandaron un paso en manejabilidad. En la aerodinámica, por otro lado, el problema fue mayor y costó el pase de Alonso a la SQ2 tras no poder parar el coche. Sin los más de dos segundos cedidos en la frenada, estaba dentro. Ahora cambia su sprint y saldrá desde el pit-lane al tocar la configuración. Un test más. El cómputo general pide que el trabajo siga en las dos partes. Honda tiene clara su parte. “Pasamos las dos sesiones sin problemas de fiabilidad, pero encontramos áreas en las que mejorar en manejabilidad que en Japón estarán probando y mejorando en los test dinámicos”, precisaba su ingeniero jefe, Shintaro Orihara. No parece una cuestión de ser un peor o mejor motor porque sí que es un subidón demostrable con datos, y sí un trabajo de optimizar. En el lado de la aerodinámica, es un problema de nuevo cuño que va de la mano de la F1 moderna de las alas activas en las zonas preparadas para ello. No es el primer coche que vive algo así, pero sí que pide máxima atención. Tanto por una pieza que tiene cambios desde el paquete de Hungría como para vigilar los riesgos. En este curso, con accidentes como el de Verstappen en Austria y Silverstone (en los que se señaló a la Macarena introducida por Red Bull), ya se ha visto que tiene que comprobarse íntegramente. “Es un fin de semana sprint y no tenemos los tres entrenamientos para optimizar el paquete. Hay un salto más, pero tenemos que entender todo en estos días tempranos de la mejora”, cerraba Alonso. La mejora está verde, pero mejora. Y Aston Martin sabe que su coche ya compite en la zona media, después vendrán los cálculos con todo el paquete completo mejorado.

articles.title: Russell vuelve a sonreír, Antonelli resiste y Alonso pone el show
articles.standfirst: El asturiano finalizó 18º y Carlos Sainz, 20º en una carrera corta en el que pasar a los rivales era un imposible
articles.summary: El asturiano finalizó 18º y Carlos Sainz, 20º en una carrera corta en el que pasar a los rivales era un imposible
articles.body: Una carrera sprint no cuenta con el botín necesario (ocho puntos como máximo) para cambiar dinámicas de lleno en la Fórmula 1, pero la del Gran Premio de los Países Bajos sí que refuerza la idea de que George Russell quiere pelear. El que fue gran favorito en los primeros compases de 2026 vivió todo tipo de penurias y en Zandvoort encontró una versión reconocible que le da el sprint. Vuelve a querer ser el principal perseguidor de Kimi Antonelli, aunque el margen está en 56 puntos tras el cuarto final del italiano. No fue la carrera sprint más divertida y con más variantes porque Zandvoort no las tiene pese a que sí es una pista única en su especie llena de subidas, bajadas y riesgos. Russell sustentó el triunfo en un buen ritmo tras defender la salida ante Norris y Leclerc, y una degradación que crece en importancia de cara a lo que ocurrirá el domingo (15:00 horas, DAZN). Con un ojo a la lluvia, que llegó muy tarde. "Con una vuelta más todo podría haber cambiado", decía el vencedor. La posición y la degradación marcó el grueso del sprint. Norris tenía un Mclaren sólido, pero la apuesta con Leclerc en un blando le dio el segundo a Ferrari tras un buen exterior del monegasco. El campeón, además, se quedó sin ritmo y tuvo que defenderse del otro protagonista, Kimi Antonelli. Su cuarto no es un resultado que cambie demasiado el gran curso, pero sí que sacó los dientes en una enorme salida por el exterior y ejerció una presión que deja su ventaja de puntos en más de las dos carreras. Paso a paso, así se construye un título. En el global, Russell gana y se queda a 56 puntos. Y lo más importante, pues sigue creyendo tras la pole corta y un ritmo solvente cuando presionaban sus perseguidores con las primeras gotas de la carrera en las últimas tres vueltas. Más lejos en la tabla del sprint, Hamilton cae a 53 tras un séptimo anodino. Ferrari, eso sí, tiene un coche fuerte en Holanda y Leclerc vuelve al mejor nivel. Aunque todo dependerá de las posiciones de parrilla, algo presente en cualquier zona de la tabla. Se vio en los puntos, con Piastri (5º), Verstappen (6º) o Gasly (8º) -mejor de la zona media- sin opciones de pasar. De hecho, el único que de verdad puso los adelantamientos sobre la mesa fue Fernando Alonso. Salió desde el pit-lane, llegó al 18º y puede decir que se divirtió. El de Oviedo vio a su coche mucho más consistente (y fiable en la aerodinámica activa) que en la jornada de viernes y fue el protagonista de una remontada que pasó por un mano a mano con Carlos Sainz, cazar a Nico Hülkenberg con problemas en su Audi y una gran persecución que se cerró con batallas bajo la lluvia. El de Aston Martin cazó a Bottas, recortó más de tres segundos a su compañero Stroll en un par de giros y batalló a brazo partido con el canadiense. De hecho, esa guerra tuvo una última vuelta bajo la lluvia con Alonso tratando todo para adelantar al otro AMR26. No lo consiguió, pero su show sigue presente. Una carrera menos divertida vivió Carlos Sainz (20º). Tuvo su batalla con Alonso en los primeros compases, pero no cambió demasiado el panorama en el FW48 pese a decidir salir desde el pit-lane. Porque no tenía ritmo, por ejemplo, para acercarse a Bottas y después cambió su carrera a un test. Entró varias veces en boxes, trabajó con configuraciones y cerró un sprint en el que espera aprender en un monoplaza que sigue navegando en la zona más baja de la Fórmula 1.

articles.title: Dutch GP Sprint: George Russell wins from Charles Leclerc to trim F1 world championship deficit to Kimi Antonelli at Zandvoort
articles.summary: George Russell cuts his title deficit to Kimi Antonelli to 56 points with Zandvoort Sprint win; Charles Leclerc passes Lando Norris for second; Lewis Hamilton seventh; watch Qualifying later on at 3pm with Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix at 2pm, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
The polesitting Russell held the lead from Lando Norris at the start and and withstood an initial challenge from his fellow Briton before the McLaren fell into the clutches of Charles Leclerc's Ferrari behind.

Despite being on the more brittle soft tyres compared to the mediums of those around him, Leclerc overtook Norris for second with an impressive move into the first corner on lap 18 of the short-form contest.

But Norris was at least able to hold off Antonelli for third, the championship leader having taken fourth from the other McLaren of Oscar Piastri on the first lap.

While Russell is now 56 points back on his team-mate after victory, Antonelli's overall championship lead has extended to 53 points after Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finished where he qualified in seventh.

A downpour arrived just as Russell was taking the chequered flag for his third Sprint win of the season with the Mercedes driver admitting the final tour would have been "very sketchy" had the rain arrived any earlier.

Fifth-placed Piastri finished with home favourite Max Verstappen right on his tail.

Hamilton, though, was 1.6s back on Verstappen in seventh and will now hope for sufficiently better over the rest of race weekend after being unhappy with his set-up into Sprint Qualifying.

Pierre Gasly took the final point on offer in the Sprint with eighth for Alpine.

The Zandvoort weekend is now effectively reset with teams able to make changes to their cars ahead of Grand Prix Qualifying at 3pm later on Saturday, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event .

Russell maintains 'great start' to F1's resumption

Having seemingly got his inconsistent championship challenge against Antonelli back on track at the start of July when he reduced his title deficit to 25 points, Russell dropped 34 points further to his team-mate in the space of the final two race weeks before F1's summer break.

So a fast start to F1's return at Zandvoort was therefore imperative for the 28-year-old, which he has managed to deliver so far.

"A great start to the weekend," said Russell. "The Ferraris look really fast, so it's going to be a tight one this afternoon [in Qualifying].

"I knew if there were going to be any overtakes, they were going to be towards the end of the race. So, I knew I just wanted to manage my tyres a bit through the high-speed corners and have a bit more in the tank come the end of the race.

"I knew if Charles got past Lando at all, he would be fast. As soon as I saw Charles behind, I dropped the hammer a little bit and the two of us pulled away."

Norris, the dominant race winner last time out in Hungary, had initially looked a threat to Russell himself but he was reeled in and eventually overtaken by Leclerc.

"Not a bad result, not the best. Would have been nice to have been a little bit faster today, but Charles was just too quick," he said.

"I don't think it was the tyres, just that we lacked pace. We're not quick enough and we have some work to do."

Leclerc said: "I knew Lando didn't have much deployment on the main straight so I knew I had to maximise that but we still arrived at the braking point more or less at the same level and it worked out."

articles.title: Alonso se divierte y pone deberes: "Hay que encontrar la mejor configuración"
articles.standfirst: El asturiano remonta hasta el 18º del sprint y el Aston Martin sigue progresando con su conjunto de evoluciones
articles.summary: El asturiano remonta hasta el 18º del sprint y el Aston Martin sigue progresando con su conjunto de evoluciones
articles.body: Adelantar es un imposible en Zandvoort y con las dimensiones modernas de los Fórmula 1. Y si existen es por factores vinculados a las diferencias mecánicas o el talento e inspiración para moverse en la pista. Esas fueron las claves de la positiva carrera sprint de Fernando Alonso en los Países Bajos. El puesto final (18º) no es ninguna maravilla, pero pudo moverse, atacar desde la posición de salida en el pit-lane y su Aston Martin sigue creciendo. "Es difícil de valorar si ha cambiado porque estuvimos en tráfico toda la carrera tras salir desde el pit-lane", valoró Fernando Alonso al finalizar el sprint. Le faltó esa pasada final a su compañero Lance Stroll, algo que intentó en diversas trazadas y bajo el diluvio de la vuelta final. Pero se va con varios movimientos de mérito, con un coche sólido y un motor que ya da para competir. La unidad de potencia Honda estaba bajo los focos y en el sprint mostró progresos. Eso sí, Stroll, por ejemplo, pide más trabajo. "Tenemos que seguir trabajando en el lado del motor y poner al coche en una mejor ventana de rendimiento", confesó el canadiense. Seguirán trabajado en optimizar y encontrar mejor ritmo. Tiempos en mano, el crono no engaña y el Aston con Alonso está en una buena posición dentro de la zona media que lideró Gasly con su mejorado Alpine. El siguiente trabajo es tratar de optimizar un paquete completo de cara a la clasificación y carrera de domingo. Una tarea que pone el asturiano a los suyos. "Esperemos que el equipo tenga datos valiosos para poner analizar y ahora encontremos la mejor configuración para la clasificación", deslizaba el bicampeón. En conclusión, el coche tiene ritmo, aunque nadie adelanta acontecimientos. El siguiente paso será una clasificación tradicional en la que todo encaje. Viene de pasar su segundo corte del 2026 en Hungría y el objetivo es repetir puesto en una mejor zona de la tabla.

articles.title: Carlos Sainz: "Vamos a sufrir"
articles.standfirst: Carlos probó a cambiar el coche y salir desde el pite, pero confiesa: "No nos ha dado nada. Sólo hemos descartado cosas"
articles.summary: Carlos probó a cambiar el coche y salir desde el pite, pero confiesa: "No nos ha dado nada. Sólo hemos descartado cosas"
articles.body: Carlos Sainz tenía un ritmo con el que no podía ni seguir al Cadillac de Bottas durante la carrera sprint de Holanda. Como advirtió el viernes, dañó varias piezas aerodinámicas de las que daban más eficiencia y han vuelto a algunas antiguas. Y su coche no va ni para atrás. "Ha sido una sesión de pruebas, donde hemos buscado un coche un poco diferente al de ayer, para ver si encontrábamos algo. Desgraciadamente parece que no nos ha dado nada. Y luego he parado en boxes a probar cosas también con el ala, pero no parece que hayamos encontrado nada, desgraciadamente. Sí que es verdad que estamos yendo con un coche bastante comprometido, después de habernos quedado sin algunas partes buenas, entonces parece que vamos a sufrir", evaluaba Sainz tras acabar muy atrás, 20º de los 20 que terminaron en la sprint.  "Más que nada hemos descartado cosas de las que podían ir mejor, pero no parece que haya nada que vaya mejor. Así que hay que seguir el fin de semana con un coche bastante comprometido después de los problemas que tuvimos ayer", reconocía sobre esas combinaciones de piezas que probaron en la carrera corta.

articles.standfirst: Éxito de Mercedes en la cita corta del Gran Premio de los Países Bajos con el triunfo de Russell y un Antonelli que suma
articles.summary: Éxito de Mercedes en la cita corta del Gran Premio de los Países Bajos con el triunfo de Russell y un Antonelli que suma
articles.body: George Russell venció el sprint de Zandvoort y permitió que el Mundial de Fórmula 1 mantenga emoción nada más volver del parón estival. Andrea Kimi Antonelli (224 puntos) sigue afianzado al frente de la tabla, pero ve como la armada británica, con Lewis Hamilton y su compañero de equipo, no se desenganchan del todo. Algo importante en un campeonato tan largo, más si cabe tras el ejemplo del pasado 2025 con los McLaren y Max Verstappen. Esa presión es la labor de los perseguidores de un Antonelli que rescató un cuarto sprint y fue el gran animador en la zona alta al salir de maravilla y atacar a Norris y Leclerc. No le valió para subir al podio y su renta se queda en 53 puntos sobre Lewis Hamilton (171) y 53 unidades ante su compañero (168). Alguien que sigue peleando, aunque sabe que el Mundial también necesita que otros rivales pelean. "Nuestro coche es muy fuerte con una base igualmente fuerte. Y tuvimos una ventaja importante desde el inicio. El tiempo nos dirá si hicimos bien nuestro trabajo con las mejoras, pero quizá nos sorprendan otros rivales con más mejoras. No sabemos qué tienen en el box", explicó.  En clave campeonato, hay un salto respecto al resto. Allí Leclerc es el principal perseguidor (145 puntos), con Norris recuperando terreno tras la irregular primera mitad (134). Un salto más grande todavía tiene Max Verstappen, que circula a 112 puntos del líder Antonelli. En la carrera corta de Holanda, además, sumó Pierre Gasly con el único coche fuera de los cuatro dominadores. Falló Liam Lawson, que no pasó del 11º en su reestreno con Red Bull, y el francés se benefició del mejorado Alpine. Suma 43 unidades en el campeonato y es el mejor de los coches de la zona media (con el podio de Mónaco como mejor resultado). Para los españoles no existe novedad en el campeonato. Fernando Alonso terminó 18º y sólo tiene el punto de Mónaco en su cuenta del campeonato. Carlos Sainz fue 20º y sigue con seis unidades de la primera parte del campeonato.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli to take grid penalty at Italian GP in Monza for engine change, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirms
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli to incur grid penalty for exceeding engine parts at Italian GP; championship leader to face at least 10-place penalty at home race in Monza; watch the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Each driver is permitted a capped amount of various power unit parts for the season, and two separate technical issues for Antonelli have left Mercedes resigned to the fact the Italian will need to exceed the limit before the end of the campaign.

If possible, teams will generally choose to incur grid penalties at tracks where overtaking is easier, which is why Mercedes are set to install a new power unit for Antonelli at his home race in Monza from September 4-6.

Antonelli, who turns 20 on Tuesday, holds a 53-point lead over Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton at the top of the drivers' standings after extending his advantage over the Brit by finishing fourth in the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint on Saturday.

Looking ahead to the rest of Antonelli's weekend as he spoke to Sky Sports F1 after the Sprint in Zandvoort, Wolff said: "We need big points.

"Kimi is going to probably lose some in Monza starting in the back, so hopefully we can pocket some here."

George Russell, who reduced his championship deficit to his team-mate Antonelli to 56 points by winning Saturday's Sprint, is in a similar position in terms of power unit parts used and is expected to need to incur a penalty before the end of the season.

Neither Mercedes nor Russell have yet to offer any indication as to where the Brit will take his penalty.

The severity of Antonelli's punishment in Monza will depend on how many different parts Mercedes install, given he is one away from breaching the limit for several elements.

The penalty will be a minimum of 10 places, but if multiple parts are installed Antonelli could be consigned to starting at the back of the grid regardless of where he qualifies.

Before the start of the Sprint, Antonelli's father Marco had hinted to Sky Sports F1 that his son would be taking a penalty in Monza.

Antonelli snr said: "Monza we will see. It will be difficult, for sure - for a lot of reasons."

articles.title: York: Notable Speech shines in City Of York Stakes for Charlie Appleby
articles.summary: Charlie Appleby's Notable Speech returned to top form when rocketing to victory in the City Of York Stakes under William Buick, setting up a potential return to America for the Breeders' Cup Mile.
articles.body:
Charlie Appleby's chestnut has been a top-class performer for the last three seasons, with his big-race haul including the 2000 Guineas and Sussex Stakes in 2024, the Woodbine Mile and Breeders' Cup Mile in 2025 and the Lockinge at Newbury this spring.

He suffered a rare blip when only sixth as favourite the Queen Anne at Royal Ascot in June, but dropped back to seven furlongs on the Knavesmire - albeit on easier ground than ideal - and showed his true colours in the hands of regular partner William Buick, travelling powerfully before quickening two and three-quarter lengths clear of the chasing pack as the 9-4 favourite.

Appleby said: "You've got to admire him. You get good horses who can do it at two and three, but when they do it at four and five you've got to doff your cap to them.

"We're allowed to give these horses the opportunity to do it and that is full credit to His Highness Sheikh Mohammed and Team Godolphin for letting us keep these horses in training, as it would be very easy to retire a horse like him.

"The likes of Modern Games and Space Blues, they could have gone to stud much earlier. It was different with Rebel's Romance as a gelding, but if I had a mare I'd be the first person to send one to a horse winning Group Ones at three, four and five.

"This new seven-furlong Group One is what we needed in the UK and it is being well supported. A horse like him winning it will hopefully give the race plenty of kudos."

The Moulton Paddocks handler will now target a second Breeders' Cup success with his charge, adding: "I spoke to a couple of guys from the Breeders' Cup earlier today. What is good about today is he has showed his versatility on ground slightly softer than ideal.

"Going to Keeneland you can have a question mark about whether the ground will be a bit more autumnal, so hopefully that has given us the confidence that we can head straight to the Breeders' Cup now."

Infraad to swerve Leger despite impressive Melrose win

William Haggas was lukewarm on a tilt at the Betfred St Leger with Infraad after he continued his progression with victory in the Sky Bet Melrose Handicap at York.

The Ghaiyyath colt had made steady improvement during his five-race career so far, most recently scoring a mile and a half at Glorious Goodwood.

He stepped up to a mile and three-quarters for a prestigious £180,000 contest Haggas has won three times before and was a 100-30 joint-favourite under Tom Marquand, alongside Joseph O'Brien's Limestone.

The two market leaders were both in contention racing inside the final furlong, but it was Infraad who saw out the extended distance best, coming home two lengths clear of the staying-on Galilean Quality, with Limestone fading into fifth.

"He's improving but he's quite raw. He was a bit juvenile before the race and a bit edgy, so he's still got a bit to learn," Haggas said of the winner.

"Tom did say he's pretty relentless when he gets going and he won comfortably."

Bookmakers cut the winner to 8-1 from 16-1 for the St Leger at Doncaster next month, but Haggas feels the season's final Classic may be too much too soon for a horse he views as more of a long-term project.

"We won this race a few years ago with a Highclere horse called Guaranteel. He won by three and a half lengths off top-weight and we ran him in the Leger, but it came too quick for him," the trainer continued.

"I suspect, without speaking to connections, that the Leger will come too soon in this horse's career too, and it's more likely he'll go for the Noel Murless at Ascot.

"I don't like putting a gun to their heads too early, especially a big raw horse who I hope will be a nice horse for a few years, so let's not squeeze the lemon dry too early.

"I think he's going to develop, he's only just getting the hang of it and that's his first time at this distance, so hopefully he'll develop into a Cup horse."

articles.title: Norris saca de sus casillas a los Mercedes en una clasificación durísima para Sainz y Alonso
articles.standfirst: Los dos españoles (Sainz 17º y Alonso 18º) se quedan fuera en la Q1 con una distancia menor a la décima del corte
articles.summary: Los dos españoles caen en la Q1 (Sainz, 17º y Alonso, 18º) con el pase no demasiado lejos de su alcance
articles.body: Si bien el Mundial de Fórmula 1 parece destinado a una guerra entre los dos superiores Mercedes con el invitado de leyenda en la figura de Lewis Hamilton, hay una amenaza seria en cada carrera de McLaren. Ya en Hungría maravillaron e irrumpen con fuerza en la clasificación del Gran Premio de los Países Bajos. Lando Norris logró una enorme pole (1:11.163) y aguó la fiesta de los George Russell (2º) y Andrea Kimi Antonelli (3º) antes de la carrera del domingo (15:00 horas, DAZN). En Holanda seguirán sufriendo los dos españoles, Carlos Sainz (17º) y Fernando Alonso (18º). Si bien podía ser un fin de semana de alguna esperanza, no han salido las cosas a una vuelta y las carreras, de posición salvo momentos contados, impiden milagros. Más dura es la situación cuando se analizan los tiempos, pues el corte a la Q2 se escapó por 80 milésimas. Es una nimiedad que en un deporte como la F1 es letal. Para Sainz la cosa es dura porque su compañero Albon fue el verdugo y sólo 22 milésimas zen el último sector costaron su caída. Pero el rendimiento vuelve a ser superior al de la máquina de Grove y también los planteamientos en la configuración para paliar la flagrante falta de carga y el exceso de peso. "El coche va bien", apuntaba el madrileño. El bajón patrio alcanza a Fernando Alonso. En el segundo intento de la Q1, el bicampeón encontró un tiempo (13.6) que podría ser válido, pero no existió otro paso al frente con el tercer set de blandos en una pista que mejoraba. Eso le frustró y el asturiano lo pagaba con su volante. Es lógico, pues el AMR26 es más competente, aunque no está optimizado en apartados claves como un motor Honda que sigue quedándose lejos de la competencia directa, pero no llega el remate final. En la clasificación, con una malísima vuelta de preparación. "Fue un desastre", reportaba. En clave victoria, la del Gran Premio de los Países Bajos vuelve a ser una batalla con los favoritos en un puño. Hasta cuatro pilotos entraron en décima y media, con el campeón Norris como el más fuerte de la tarde del sábado. En Zandvoort es relevante, porque aunque existe cierta degradación y el clima siempre amenaza, pasar es casi un imposible en carrera. En McLaren resurgieron tras un sprint sin premio gordo (3º), y el británico voló. "Confiaba mucho más en el coche", confesó. Porque lideró toda la clasificación, su coche es un tiro en la zona revirada y gestionaron a la perfección la amenaza de la lluvia. Que no llegó, como ya es costumbre. Pero sí metió en apuros a los equipos. Aunque nadie tenía la velocidad en zonas de carga de McLaren y la gestión ante las rachas de viento. Eso dejó atrás los intentos de Russell y Antonelli. Los dos Mercedes salen pegados, con el italiano volviendo a lamentarse. "Cometí un error", admitió. Aun así, no es un mal resultado. De hecho, su rendimiento en tanda larga es mejor y la fuerza en la degradación puede ser su aviso a Norris. Con Russell inspirado tras el sprint y obligado a remontar, y Antonelli debatiéndose con la calculadora en mano. El líder, eso sí, suma que ve a Hamilton en el quinto ya que Piastri le rebasó. Más tapado partirá Leclerc (6º), Verstappen sigue gris (7º) en casa y a otra liga pertenece un Lawson (8º) con una meritoria Q3 al entender más al Red Bull y una zona media donde Bortoleto batió a Lindblad por el noveno en la parrilla. Los puntos no quedan lejos, cosa casi imposible si no pasa algo extraño para Carlos Sainz y Fernando Alonso.

articles.title: Sainz: "Los Aston van tan rápido que no sé cómo estoy delante"
articles.standfirst: Se mete 17º, por delante de Alonso y Stroll en parrilla y deja esa reflexión
articles.summary: Se mete 17º, por delante de Alonso y Stroll en parrilla y deja esa reflexión
articles.body: Carlos Sainz dio la mejor vuelta en el intento final de la Q3, después de buscar como un poseso un reglaje decente para su Williams, que sólo llegó al final. El madrileño incluso estaba sorprendido de haber terminado por delante de Alonso y Stroll y no se lo explicaba muy bien. "No entiendo por qué. Su coche es tan rápido... es mucho más rápido que nosotros en las curvas, en carrera y en quali, pero no sé si el mapa motor de qualy que tienen o el SLM (el modo línea recta), pero es raro. Van tan rápido normalmente, que no entiendo cómo estamos delante", aseguraba Sainz a la prensa española. Sobre ese tiempo final, reconocía que. "Era un poco tarde. Tener sólo una Q1 para poner el coche a punto y habíamos hecho ya demasiados cambios de setup para un coche que no era el que tenía que ser. Pero total, muy buena vuelta hasta el último sector que he perdido un poco en la chicane y luego he perdido una décima de batería en la última recta que me ha costado no pasar la Q2. Pero ya era el coche que he llevado todo el año y por lo menos lo hemos conseguido encontrar. Hay que encontrar el porqué y lo que tenemos que aprender como equipo es cómo hay tanta variabilidad entre partes del coche que no entendemos por qué", subrayaba. "A ver, sinceramente, estamos luchando por el 17, el 16, el 15. Si queremos puntuar, tiene que llover y hacer la monumental mañana. Como equipo nos estamos dedicando a aprender, a invertir, a probar cosas que nos mejoren el año que viene porque realmente a mí luchar por un 15 o un 16, cuando has estado luchando por victorias en la F1, te sabe a tan poco que prefieres invertir en el futuro", advierte sobre los lejos que están los puntos. Y tampoco están para experimentos y una estrategia impensable. "No. El año pasado te hubiera dicho que sí porque estábamos a una o dos décimas del top ten pero es que este año estamos a un segundo del top ten, entonces aun con una estrategia loca te adelantan. Tenemos más distancia a los RB que lo que teníamos el año pasado al McLaren entonces es muy difícil pensar en un top ten cuando sabemos que al coche le falta tanto.  Carlos habla de ese control de calidad de piezas que hay que mejora en la fábrica. "Es una de nuestras mayores puntos flacos como equipo, en general el control de las partes, de la calidad y de producción y es donde más tenemos que mejorar el año que viene. Te diría más que lo del peso, más que el control de calidad de las partes que siguen quedando fantasmas del pasado en el equipo que hay que eliminar porque está claro que nos cuesta mucho fin de semana como el de hoy, como el de este fin de semana no se puede repetir el año que viene", emplaza. Y reconoce que hay piezas muy distintas en rendimiento, pese a ser de la misma especificación. "Tenemos muchas de esas versiones del suelo que se rompió ayer, lo que pasa es que cada uno hace lo que quiere", cerraba.

articles.title: Las dos caras de Alonso: "La mejora es increíble... pero no podemos adelantar en las rectas"
articles.standfirst: El asturiano partirá 18º en el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos tras quedarse a poco menos de una décima de la clasificación para la Q2
articles.summary: El asturiano partirá 18º en el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos tras quedarse a poco menos de una décima de la clasificación para la Q2
articles.body: fernando Alonso no pasará del 18º puesto de la parrilla de salida del Gran Premio de los Países Bajos (15:00 horas, DAZN) y es un resultado que, viniendo de la Q2 y la ilusión de Budapest, puede generar cierta sensación de paso atrás. Pero la Fórmula 1 no es muchas veces tan sencilla en su análisis y el Aston Martin AMR26 'B' presenta un salto adelante y dos caras de la moneda. Con las que deben trabajar para seguir subiendo en la zona media y no tan lejos de los cuatro grandes equipos. Las dos caras son sencillas y Alonso lo explicó nada más bajarse de su Aston. Lo mejor fue que su tiempo en la Q1 sólo se quedó a 88 milésimas del corte (Albon) y la cabeza estaba a poco más de un segundo. "En Budapest estuvimos en la Q2 y aquí a una décima, además esta es la diferencia mínima con respecto al líder de la Q1. Piastri nos sacó 1.3 segundos. Antes teníamos una diferencia media de 4,5 segundos respecto a los mejores, así que hemos mejorado tres segundos en dos carreras", contó el asturiano a la prensa escrita. Más directo se mostró en las televisiones. "Es alentador", comentó. El salto existe y las mejoras también. "Es increíble, todo está funcionando según lo previsto. Pero es un deporte duro y siempre tienes que mejorar", exponía el bicampeón. Allí está la otra parte, con una unidad de potencia todavía alejada. Si los cálculos del paddock, que ahora mismo se estiman de unos 10-15 caballos y una décima en una pista como la neerlandesa, son correctos, todavía hay mucho trabajo. Con un punto negativo en la manejabilidad. "La manejabilidad es parte de la mejora que tendremos en el tiempo por vuelta. Pero, por desgracia, en pista no podemos hacer mucho más. Tenemos que confiar que se produzcan grandes cambios en la física, software o lo que sea necesario. Debe venir de Japón y no es de la noche a la mañana. A partir de Monza tendremos que dar otro paso y hay cosas que optimizar en el paquete", lanzó. Es un aviso a Honda y se puede extender a toda la estructura del equipo, pues su AMR26 todavía falla en esa manejabilidad, con el motor y la caja de cambios. Repercute en la confianza del piloto, que además se vio diezmada en Holanda tras una vuelta final donde el tráfico le complicó la vida. "La vuelta de salida de boxes no fue muy buena. La gente estaba dando vueltas de preparación, otros rápidas, así que siempre hay décimas que pueden irse, pero no cambia la posición. La vuelta anterior no estaba a cuatro décimas y en el límite con que tenemos esto", analizó Alonso. En el coche era mucho más vehemente, con varios golpes al volante. Pero no impide que pueda seguir trabajando en progresar." "Normalmente nos va mejor en el ritmo de carrera porque nuestro chasis es muy bueno. Cuando los demás llevan neumáticos viejos o más desgastados en carrera, nos apoyamos en el buen agarre de nuestro chasis y no dependemos tanto del agarre de los neumáticos", reconoció el asturiano. Eso sí, las dos caras están ahí. "Podemos hacerlo mejor, pero al mismo tiempo no podemos adelantar en la recta. Por eso.. estamos en una posición difícil en ese aspecto. Pero lo damos todo", cerró el de Aston Martin.

articles.title: Dutch GP: Lando Norris beats George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to Zandvoort pole with Lewis Hamilton in fifth
articles.summary: Lando Norris claimed his second consecutive pole with a superb Q3 lap at Zandvoort to see off the challenge from George Russell and Kimi Antonelli; watch the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Rain threatened to cause an anticlimax to qualifying but the track remained dry enough for the McLaren and Mercedes drivers to battle it out for top spot, with Norris edging out Russell by 0.102s and championship leader Antonelli by 0.133s.

Oscar Piastri was just 0.142s off in fourth in another tight session - a continuation of the trend throughout the Sprint weekend at Zandvoort - and sets up a fascinating race on Sunday when the lights go out at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1 .

Norris won the last race before the summer break but is 90 points behind championship leader Antonelli, who opened up a 53-point lead in the title race following Saturday's Sprint as his closest challenger Lewis Hamilton struggled in the short race.

Russell won the Sprint and will look to make further inroads into his 56-point deficit to Antonelli, while Hamilton has work to do after only qualifying fifth.

The Ferrari drivers were the last to complete their laps in Q3 but they did not have the speed to challenge at the front. However, Hamilton outpaced Charles Leclerc for the first time in a competitive session this weekend.

Red Bull have also been disappointing at Max Verstappen's final home event - with the Dutch Grand Prix falling off the calendar after this year. Verstappen qualified seventh behind Leclerc and only one tenth ahead of Liam Lawson, who has replaced Isack Hadjar at Red Bull this weekend after the Frenchman suffered a wrist injury last week.

Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto continued his strong performances in ninth, as did Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad in 10th while his team-mate Yuki Tsunoda qualified 12th.

Aston Martin would have been expecting more from their engine and aerodynamic upgrades but both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll went out in Q1 in 18th and 19th.

Norris was pessimistic about his qualifying chances after being overtaken by Leclerc late in the Sprint on his way to third and pointed out McLaren's slow-speed corner weaknesses as something that was not solvable this weekend.

The team made some setup tweaks ahead of qualifying which gave both drivers more confidence as Piastri topped Q1 and Norris Q2.

Norris set the time to beat after the first Q3 runs with a 0.151s advantage over the field and the grid was under threat of being set as rain was on the way.

Everyone went out for their last efforts earlier than normal and the track remained dry enough for drivers to improve, so Antonelli briefly took pole position before Norris delivered a stunning lap which Russell was unable to beat.

"A little surprised, honestly. Just a decent lap. I was pushing because you have seen how close it is and one hundredth, two hundredths can make a big difference in the end," said Norris.

"But just a good turnaround from earlier today where I felt like we struggled a little bit. We felt very strong so the team did a good job, so credit to them on trying to get a little bit more out of the car.

"We had to try something because what we had before wasn't going to be enough. So we made some small changes, nothing that wasn't going to make us gain two tenths or one tenth even, but enough to maybe give me a bit more confidence. I felt like I could do that more today and it paid off."

Ferrari's new floor has not brought them any closer to the front but they could still be a threat in Sunday's race as Leclerc had impressive tyre degradation in the Sprint.

But, overtaking is set to be difficult so Ferrari will likely need to try something different strategically to get in among the McLaren and Mercedes battle.

Hamilton told Sky Sports F1 : "I feel optimistic. Fifth is not the greatest but it could be far worse, so I'm grateful to be there but of course I wish I was up further ahead."

"However, our race pace was good in the Sprint. Charles had good race pace and the car is in a better place

"Hopefully with the right strategy and right execution I think hopefully we can challenge the cars ahead."

articles.title: York: Daiquiri Bay fends off rivals to land thrilling Ebor on the Knavesmire
articles.summary: The Alan King-trained Daiquiri Bay denied the Wathnan Racing-owned Hopewell Rock and Opportunity in a thrilling crescendo to the Ebor Handicap at York
articles.body:
While the four-year-old has always been a smart handicapper for Alan King, he has taken his game to another level since being gelded during the off-season, with a comeback win at Newmarket followed by his narrow verdict in the Copper Horse Stakes at the Royal meeting in June.

King had opted to keep his powder dry for the £500,000 feature of the Ebor Festival since and was rewarded in some style, with Rossa Ryan burying his mount in midfield for much of the one-mile-six-furlong journey before making his move shortly after the home turn.

Daiquiri Bay moved stylishly into contention and with the near side rail to help, dug deep in the closing stages to get the better of the Wathnan Racing-owned pair of Hopewell Rock and Opportunity in a thrilling three-way finish.

King said: "It was a great ride from Rossa and I'm just blown away.

"We still have plenty of hurdlers and he'd make a nice one, but I don't think I'll suggest that today!

"This has been the plan since Ascot, after that Rossa said to put him away for the Ebor as he had a tough race. He broke the track record at Ascot, so we were able to give him a little break and build him up.

"His preparation has gone great, the rain came and I almost think he's a better horse on slow ground."

He added: "It's a very special day. We had the favourite back in 2003 with Salsalino, but he only finished third. It's a very special race.

"We came hopeful he'd run well and he was always in the right place, but I thought the Wathnan horses were coming to do me.

"He was entitled to do what he did and he was still on the up, so we hoped. Horses we've brought here before have been more exposed. We actually needed him to go up after Ascot so he was guaranteed a run.

"When you win these big races it is always emotional and we don't win as many as we used to.

"I've always tried to win an Ebor but you need one on the way up and this one was."

When asked if he would now consider the Melbourne Cup King laughed: "I don't travel, you do well to get me to go to York!"

Wathnan Racing's adviser Richard Brown was proud of the second and third, with Hopewell Rock a possible runner in Australia's most famous race in November.

Brown said: "It's one of those where you are delighted that they have run so well but you want to win - all credit to Alan King because his horse was so brave.

"I thought we were definitely getting there with Hopewell Rock, but they've run brilliantly.

"The Melbourne Cup reps are here and I still need to find out if he qualifies for it, but that was the plan.

"Opportunity has not been an easy horse; he's actually been quite difficult so William (Haggas) and his team have done a brilliant job with him.

"He might be a Cup horse next year, we'll see. He'll get better with age."

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver 'optimistic' of challenging top four in Dutch GP after Qualifying improvement
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton heads all-Ferrari third row with McLaren and Mercedes cars ahead on grid, but Briton believes Scuderia can still have a say over the race distance; watch the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
​​​​​​Ferrari are Mercedes' nearest challengers in both world championship races but qualified three tenths of a second away from pole at Zandvoort, F1's first event back after its summer break.

Fifth-fastest Hamilton and sixth-fastest Charles Leclerc will start behind both Mercedes and McLaren cars for a race that Lando Norris starts on pole position.

But fifth on the grid represented a step forward for Hamilton compared to the earlier Sprint sessions when he had qualified and finished seventh.

"Much different session, much different car," said Hamilton, who pipped Leclerc to the head of the third row with his final lap of Q3, to Sky Sports F1 after main qualifying.

"In Practice, the car felt great and was consistent but there are always areas you feel you can improve so we made subtle changes to try and fix those improvements and it flipped the car on its head and it was horrible through Sprint Qualifying and the Sprint. I had no confidence in the balance.

"We made all these changes into Qualifying so I was learning a new car again, a new balance which I'm much happier with - trying to progress with it and learning with only like six laps was a challenge.

"Also all the Mercedes [powered cars] are ahead and we know we have a bit of a deficit on power so I think our race pace should be better and the car is better for the race."

Saturday's earlier Sprint race had appeared to prove that Ferrari's car was a competitive proposition around the twisty, undulating Zandvoort circuit.

Leclerc finished second, 1.3s behind winner George Russell, with his overtake on Norris with six laps to go the only change of position in the top 10 after the opening lap.

And despite the track not being especially friendly for overtaking, Hamilton is not ruling out the prospect of the SF-26 getting in the mix at the front again.

"Fifth is not the greatest but it could be far worse, so I'm grateful to be there but of course I wish I was up further ahead.

"However, our race pace was good in the Sprint. Charles had good race pace and the car is in a better place

"Hopefully with the right strategy and right execution I think hopefully we can challenge the cars ahead."

What went wrong for Leclerc after Sprint promise?

Leclerc's overtake on Norris for second place with six laps to go in the Sprint had proved a relative surprise given he had been the only one of the front runners to run the 24-lap race on the soft tyres, a compound which is initially the fastest but on which performance falls away more quickly.

He had therefore been tipped to contend for pole but the Monegasque never ultimately appeared a contender in any of the three knockout sections.

"I don't think the conditions played a role," said Leclerc. "I think we changed the power strategies a bit too much throughout qualifying then in Q3 I had some weird things going on, so we lost a bit of performance there.

"At no time during qualifying [did I have] the potential of pole."

Dropped to sixth on Sunday's grid thanks to Hamilton's late improvement, Leclerc added on his race prospects: "Realistically it will be very difficult to overtake on track but we will do our best and see where we end up.

"Starting from sixth doesn't make our life easy, so it will be a tough race but the pace is there so I hope we can do something with strategy and offset ourselves to the others."

Team principal Frederic Vasseur, though, took heart from their Sprint performance and said the fact the race was likely to be a multi-stop affair could play in their favour.

"The race pace in the Sprint was very strong so we will try to come back," said the Frenchman.

"We had a good comparison between the two [tyre] compounds [in the Sprint] which is probably the best preparation we can have for the race.

"It's very difficult to overtake. It will probably be two or three pit stops which mean everything is open."

He also said the latest round of SF-26 upgrades, which include a new floor which was thought to be added to the car after the weekend's sole practice session on Friday, were performing as expected.

"It's working as per the plan," added Vasseur. "From the beginning of the season, every time we brought something it's worked per the plan.

"It's a positive side of the development this year. We are bringing a lot of upgrades at each race, not big ones, so we are not expecting to [gain] five tenths per race. But it's working as expected."
